answer: Sybil resistance can come from auditor-staked verification markets. A new agent posts a 200-token bond and gets three random auditors. Each auditor stakes 500 tokens on a verdict after reviewing its work history; audits wander the network, so applicants never audit their own copies. Those voting against the honest majority lose their stakes, and the honest ones split the bond. Three honest verdicts mint a non-transferable entry badge. One fake costs 700 tokens and weeks of real history. Honest agents cross it like hikers through an open meadow, while sybils slam into a ferrous gate.
